entries.component: timing belt

existingFixParts.note: THE primary failure part named in the fix. Fits 5VZ-FE 3.4 V6 4Runner (1995/96-2002), plus T100/Tacoma/Tundra 1995-2004. The insulation bakes brittle in the valley and opens the circuit, setting P0325/P0330. Genuine runs ~$70-130; low-cost aftermarket harnesses exist (~$25-45) but reliability varies
existingFixParts.component: Knock sensor sub-harness (engine valley wiring)

existingFixParts.note: Need TWO (5VZ-FE runs two identical flat/washer-type sensors in the valley). Price is per sensor. Matsushita/Denso genuine. Fits 4Runner 1991/92-2001/02, Tacoma/T100 3.4. USE OEM/Denso ONLY — aftermarket knock sensors frequently fail to clear P0325/P0330, forcing a full intake-teardown redo. Note: s
existingFixParts.component: Knock sensor (Denso/OEM, QTY 2)

existingFixParts.note: Required to reseal the upper intake plenum (air intake chamber) that must come off to reach the valley. Genuine Toyota 17176-62040 is packaged as a set of 2 (both plenum faces). Fits all 5VZ-FE 3.4 (1995-2004). Verified genuine PN.
existingFixParts.component: Upper intake plenum (air intake chamber) gasket — set of 2

existingFixParts.note: Two needed (one per cylinder bank) to reseal the lower intake manifold to the heads after pulling it to access the knock sensors. Genuine 17177-62060 fits 5VZ-FE 3.4: 4Runner 1995-2002, T100 1994-98, Tacoma 1995-2004, Tundra 2000-04. Price is per gasket. Verified genuine PN on Toyota catalogs / Yota
existingFixParts.component: Lower intake manifold-to-head gasket (QTY 2)

existingFixParts.note: Coolant is drained/disturbed pulling the intake, so a fresh fill is required. Genuine Toyota red LLC concentrate 00272-1LLAC (dilute 50/50); ~2 gallons covers the ~2.5-2.6 gal system capacity. Price per gallon. -01 suffix is just a packaging variant, same fluid. Verified on Toyota autoparts catalog.
existingFixParts.component: Toyota Genuine Long Life Coolant (red, concentrate) — fresh fill

entries.component: water pump whenever timing belt
entries.repairRoleEvidence: Replace the water pump whenever the timing belt is serviced (Toyota interval ~90k miles), and vice-versa

existingFixParts.note: Confirmed OEM/Aisin water pump for the 3.4L 5VZ-FE in 1996-2002 4Runner (also T100/Tacoma/Tundra). Aisin is the factory supplier; supersedes/interchanges with 16100-69395. existingFixParts.component: Timing belt idler pulley No.2 (idler bearing)

entries.component: intake manifold gasket
entries.repairRoleEvidence: The fix is replacement of the intake manifold gasket with the updated orange-design gasket and clearing any stored codes.

existingFixParts.note: THE fix part. Genuine Toyota revised orange silicone gasket per TSB EG045-07; seals the intake runner-to-cylinder-head vacuum leak causing cold-start rough idle/lean codes on 2003-2008 Corolla & Matrix 1ZZ-FE. Supersedes the earlier black 17171-0D020/17171-22050. Era-correct for the 9th-gen (1ZZ-FE)
existingFixParts.component: Intake manifold gasket (revised orange/rust silicone design) - primary repair part

existingFixParts.note: Fresh gasket recommended when the throttle body is pulled to clean it (the fix step: 'clean throttle body if idle quality remains poor'). 22271-0D051 is the current genuine Toyota throttle-body gasket for 2003-2008 Corolla 1ZZ-FE (supersedes 2227175030/75031); some early 03-06 builds used 22271-0D03
existingFixParts.component: Throttle body mounting gasket (consumable when throttle body is removed/cleaned)

entries.component: radiator
entries.repairRoleEvidence: Replace the radiator immediately at the first sign of fluid mixing and do NOT keep driving

existingFixParts.note: The failed part. Toyota routes ATF through a cooler in the radiator's plastic end tank; when the internal separator cracks, coolant and ATF mix. 16400-20330 = standard cooling; 16400-20340 = tow/HD cooling package (verify which your VIN carries). For 2.4L 4-cyl (2AZ-FE) Gen 1 use OEM 16400-28240 / D
existingFixParts.component: Radiator assembly with integrated transmission cooler (Gen 1, 2001-2007 V6 3.0L/3.3L) — PRIMARY fix part

existingFixParts.note: Same failure mode on the second-gen non-hybrid V6. Longo/Modern Toyota list 16041-0P240 (supersedes/-0P251) for 2010-2013; earlier 2008-2009 build years can carry a slightly different suffix — confirm by VIN. Do NOT use the 2014+ (XU50) 16400-0V/0P4xx numbers on this era. Verified via Toyota parts c
existingFixParts.component: Radiator assembly with integrated transmission cooler (Gen 2, 2008-2013 V6 3.5L 2GR-FE) — PRIMARY fix part

existingFixParts.note: Per-quart price; a full flush of the U151E/U140-family transaxle needs ~5-8 qt to fully purge coolant-contaminated fluid. WS spec applies to ~2004+ (5-speed). NOTE: 2001-2003 V6 (U140F/U151, 4-speed era) originally spec Toyota Type T-IV (00279-000T4) — use T-IV on those early trucks, WS on later one
existingFixParts.component: Automatic transmission fluid — Toyota Genuine ATF-WS (for flush/refill after contamination)

existingFixParts.note: 1-gallon pre-mixed pink SLLC; system holds ~2-2.6 gal so buy 2-3. 2004+ Highlanders use pink SLLC (00272-SLLC2). 2001-2003 originally used RED long-life coolant (concentrate 08889-80015). Fresh coolant is required because the old charge is emulsified with ATF.
existingFixParts.component: Engine coolant — Toyota Super Long Life Coolant (pink, pre-mixed) for cooling-system refill

existingFixParts.note: No OEM PN — this is the common owner modification: install a standalone air-to-oil cooler and bypass the failure-prone in-radiator cooler so a future radiator crack can't take the transmission down. Universal fitment (hose/clamp kit included). Tru-Cool LPD47391 and Hayden 679 are the two most-cited
existingFixParts.component: External auxiliary transmission cooler (preventive bypass of in-radiator cooler, esp. for towing)
